column1: Will 22 internal links move the needle?
column2: YES — but only combined with external backlinks. Internal links distribute existing authority. If the Texas state page has zero external backlinks, internal links alone won't rank it. Think of internal links as 'connecting the pipes' — you still need water (external authority) flowing in.

Section 6 (route card titles) and Section 20 (nearby states). These create the hub-and-spoke topology Google rewards. The Texas page becomes an authority hub linking down to specific routes and across to neighboring state hubs.

The Pennsylvania map included a 'Popular Shipping Routes' section (section 20 in PA) with 5 dedicated route cards. For Texas, the route card titles in section 6 already serve this purpose since they link to the same state-to-state pages. Adding a duplicate 'Popular Routes' section would be redundant.

FAQ answers are stored in the backend API (data.faq_1 through faq_8) and rendered as raw HTML. Links MUST be added in the API/database content, NOT in the frontend component. The FAQSection component just renders whatever HTML it receives.

column1: Should we add more links later?
column2: Not on this page. 22 links is already generous. Over-linking dilutes equity per link. Focus additional linking effort on the ROUTE pages (texas-to-california, texas-to-florida, etc.) which are the actual money pages that convert visitors to leads.
